open_points.subject: concurrent publication and replay
open_points.text: A07 says “Two concurrent publishes of a type are both accepted with consecutive versions”; A01 says a repeated publish with the same request id returns one existing pointer and makes no version.
open_points.question: Does A07's two-publication rule apply only when the concurrent calls carry different request ids?
options: Only different request ids create consecutive versions
Even the same request id creates two versions when concurrent
open_points.default_guess: Qualify A07: concurrent publishes with distinct request ids create consecutive versions; equal request ids are one A01 replay.

open_points.subject: linearization of agent-authority reads
open_points.text: “A call whose transaction commits before the change is accepted, one that commits after it is checked against the changed session” does not say where a read-only call, which stores nothing, commits or is ordered against a revocation, archive or session end.
open_points.question: At what point is a read-only agent-authority call linearized against concurrent access changes?
options: At the authorization-and-read snapshot in one read transaction
When the response is completed
At request start
open_points.default_guess: Perform authorization and the read in one transaction and linearize it at that transaction's snapshot.

open_points.subject: new owner session idle deadline
open_points.text: The session ends after “30 minutes without an owner request”, while an owner request is defined as carrying an already-valid session; the text does not set the initial last-request instant when sign-in creates the session.
open_points.question: From what instant does the 30-minute idle limit run before the session's first post-sign-in request?
options: The successful sign-in instant
The first post-sign-in request
No idle expiry until a post-sign-in request occurs
open_points.default_guess: Initialize the last-request instant to the successful sign-in instant.

open_points.subject: pending confirmation values
open_points.text: M11 now says “its pending confirmation values ... each kept until used, replaced or the session ends”, but no rule states how many may coexist or what event replaces one.
open_points.question: May one owner session hold several live confirmation values, and if so, which existing value is replaced when another confirmation step is shown?
options: Several may coexist; only a new value for the same action and target replaces the old one
Only one may exist; every new confirmation step replaces it
Several may coexist and none is replaced before use, expiry or session end
open_points.default_guess: Allow several, keyed by action and target, with a newly shown step replacing the prior value for that same action and target.

open_points.subject: uploaded import file lifetime after a refused confirmation
open_points.text: M11 now says the import file is kept “until used”, while A16 says it is kept “until the import is confirmed” and A13 consumes a confirmation value on a refused submission.
open_points.question: Does a confirmation submission that passes session and CSRF checks but is later refused also drop the uploaded import file?
options: Keep the file after a refused confirmation; drop it only after an accepted import, replacement or session end
Drop the file on the first confirmation submission, accepted or refused
open_points.default_guess: Keep the file after refusal and drop it only after successful import, replacement or session end.

open_points.subject: failure precedence within an A04 stage
open_points.text: A04 orders stages (1) through (6), but within stages it groups multiple checks—such as several invalid values in stage (4), or archived, erased, customer eligibility and conflicts in stage (6)—without ordering them.
open_points.question: When two checks in the same stage fail, which failure is the operation's answer?
options: Declare a fixed order for every check within each stage
Declare all failures within a stage observationally identical
Allow operation-specific ordering stated with each operation
open_points.default_guess: Give each operation a fixed check order within every stage.

open_points.subject: import preview workflow
open_points.text: A16 says uploading the file “answers the mapping” and that this mapping already includes the projects the owner picks, their new names and aliases, and Customer values the owner gives, without saying whether those choices accompany upload or are submitted afterward.
open_points.question: What exact request sequence produces the final mapping that the confirmation value binds?
options: Upload first produces a raw preview; a later owner submission supplies picks and values and produces the confirmable mapping
The upload request itself carries all picks, names, aliases and Customer values
The server maintains an editable mapping across multiple requests
open_points.default_guess: Upload the file first, then submit picks and values to produce one final confirmation preview.

open_points.subject: validation scope when picked and unpicked records collide
open_points.text: A16 says records of unpicked projects are “neither checked nor imported”, but malformedness includes duplicate ids among the file's records and rule 1 shows “every id that conflicts”; a duplicate or conflict may involve one picked and one unpicked record.
open_points.question: Does an unpicked record participate in duplicate-id, reference and production-conflict checks when it collides with a picked record?
options: Ignore it completely, so only the picked subgraph is validated
Use it to detect ambiguity or collision affecting a picked record
Validate all identifiers in the file but import only picked records
open_points.default_guess: Ignore records wholly outside the picked subgraph, but refuse when they make the identity of a picked record ambiguous.

open_points.subject: imported customer identity handling
open_points.text: M04 says every distinct v1 customer value makes a new Customer with a newly minted customer_ref, while A16 treats “a Registry-minted customer_ref production holds” as a possible incoming conflict and also calls a record malformed when it names a customer “the file does not hold”.
open_points.question: Does the VPS import ever preserve an incoming customer_ref or require Customer records in the file, or does every distinct v1 value always generate a new Customer as M04 says?
options: Always mint a new Customer for every distinct v1 value; no incoming customer identity is preserved
Recognize and preserve some incoming Registry-minted customer_ref values
Require explicit Customer records and decide preservation from those records
open_points.default_guess: Follow M04: group projects by distinct v1 value and mint one new Customer for each group.

open_points.subject: valid imported pointer history
open_points.text: A16 refuses “more than one” published pointer and requires a superseded pointer to be lower than a later version, but does not require the highest version to be the sole published pointer or every lower version to be superseded.
open_points.question: Which status sequence is valid for an imported 1..n pointer history when withdrawn pointers are forbidden?
options: Versions 1..n-1 must be superseded and version n must be published
Any sequence with at most one published pointer and the stated local checks is valid
No published pointer is also allowed
open_points.default_guess: Require versions 1..n-1 to be superseded and version n to be published.

open_points.subject: temporal consistency of imported histories
open_points.text: A16 checks only that records were not changed, archived or superseded before creation, addition or publication; it does not state whether an archived project's archived instant equals its last-changed instant, whether a superseded instant equals the next publication instant, or whether rooms and pointers may appear after project archival.
open_points.question: Which cross-record and equal-instant constraints must an imported history satisfy?
options: Enforce all transition invariants implied by State 1 and A07
Check only the inequalities explicitly listed in A16
Ignore source history consistency beyond parseable instants
open_points.default_guess: Enforce the normal transition invariants: archival equals the project's final change, supersession coincides with the replacing publish, and no room or pointer operation occurs after archival.

open_points.subject: backup run missed at 03:00 UTC
open_points.text: A18 says Registry backs up “once a day at 03:00 UTC” and retries failures “at the next run”, but says nothing about a process that is stopped at 03:00, starts after 03:00, or restarts several times in one day.
open_points.question: When is a missed daily run performed, and how is a second run on the same UTC day prevented?
options: Run once immediately after startup if today's scheduled run was missed, recording the last completed attempt durably
Skip the day and wait for the next 03:00 UTC
Run at every startup after 03:00 UTC
open_points.default_guess: Persist the last scheduled run attempted and perform one catch-up run after startup when today's run was missed.

open_points.subject: retention invariant after deletion failure
open_points.text: Rule 6 says a deletion may fail and is retried at the next run, while the formal invariant says “after a run: no backup older than 30 days exists”.
open_points.question: What guarantee holds when deleting an expired backup fails?
options: The old backup may remain and the invariant is conditional on successful deletion
Registry must keep retrying during the same run until no expired backup remains
A deletion failure stops serving until retention is restored
open_points.default_guess: Allow the expired backup to remain, report it, and make the invariant conditional on successful deletion.

open_points.subject: failed backup verification whose deletion also fails
open_points.text: A backup that fails its check “is deleted”, but rule 6 allows deletion to fail, while the formal invariant says every kept backup is checked and valid.
open_points.question: What state and classification does an invalid backup have if Registry cannot delete its file?
options: Quarantine and exclude it from the set of backups, then retry deletion
Keep it as a backup despite failed verification
Stop serving until it can be removed
open_points.default_guess: Mark or rename it as quarantined, never treat it as a restorable backup, and retry deletion later.

open_points.subject: security-review catalogue
open_points.text: A21 says the review uses “the nine of the Workbench's security review (`skills/spec-authoring/SECURITY_REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md`)” but the category definitions and completion criteria are not contained in the accepted texts.
open_points.question: What exact questions or evidence criteria must be satisfied for each category to justify the stated APPLICABLE or NOT_APPLICABLE outcome?
options: Include the nine category definitions and evidence criteria in these texts
Treat the listed labels and outcomes as assertions requiring no reproducible criteria
Make the referenced catalogue a normative dependency shipped with the specification
open_points.default_guess: Include the category definitions and evidence criteria in the accepted design so the review can be reproduced.
